To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bound-electron nonlinearities play a dominant role in low-order harmonic emission from noble gases at intensities lower than 100 TW/cm ², while at higher pump intensities the tunnel-ionization currents are more effective in the generation of low-order harmonics.

low-order harmonic generation can be enhanced by a factor of 10 in noble gases in the tunnel-ionization regime by using pump laser pulses with an optimal intensity of about 200 TW/cm², where the main contributions to low-order harmonically generated light originate either from the bound electron nonlinearity or tunnel-ionization current.

the optimum intensity of the pump pulses in the tunnel-ionization regime is about 100 TW cm² for noble gases and the efficiency of the VUV generation can be increased by using the bound-electron susceptibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the pump laser pulse parameters in order to achieve the highest efficiency of low-order harmonic generation.
the combined action of the bound electron nonlinearity and tunnel ionization in low-order harmonic emission from noble gases.
the influence of the bound-electrons nonlinearity on low-order harmonic generation and the possibility to generate VUV pulses by using the tunnel-ionization mechanism in the noble gases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for the optimum pump intensity in argon, the phase-mismatched harmonic generation is mainly due to the bound-electron nonlinearities, while for the high pump intensity, the phase-matching is achieved due to the tunnel-ionization currents.
in noble gases the bound-electron contribution to the harmonic generation dominates at low intensities, whereas the tunnel-ionization process takes the leading role at high pump intensities.

for noble gases the bound-electron contributions to low-order harmonic generation are significant, and the phase mismatching caused by the plasma can be reduced by the use of longer pump wavelengths and lower intensities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase-mismatched plasma-induced harmonic generation in noble gas targets can be efficiently enhanced by increasing the pump intensity.

for noble gases, the optimum pump intensity for the maximum harmonic efficiency is much lower than for the case of atomic gases, which can be explained by the fact that in the latter case the tunneling ionized electrons play the main role in harmonic generation, which requires higher pump intensities.
the bound-electron contribution to low-order harmonic generation is important even for intensities of about 300 TW/cm ², which is much higher than those used in most recent experiments.
